Check the Expected Features of an Argument

Source: R/arg_check.R
arg_check.Rd

Checks the expected features of an object, typically an argument of a function: class, type, mode, length, allowed values, and for numeric data, proportions, negative values, infinite values and integers stored as double. The problems detected are returned, not raised as errors (except for data made of NA only).

Usage

arg_check(
  data,
  class = NULL,
  typeof = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  length = NULL,
  prop = FALSE,
  options = NULL,
  double_as_integer_allowed = FALSE,
  all_options_in_data = FALSE,
  na_contain = FALSE,
  neg_values = TRUE,
  inf_values = TRUE,
  print = FALSE,
  data_name = NULL,
  data_arg = TRUE,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

data

Object to test. It cannot be made of NA only (error, as for every argument of the safer-r functions), whatever na_contain.

class

Vector of character strings, compared exactly (same values, in the same order) to class(data): e.g., class = c("matrix", "array") for matrices and class = c("ordered", "factor") for ordered factors. NULL: class not tested.

typeof

Single character string, compared to typeof(data). Several values always give a problem, since typeof(data) is a single string. NULL: type not tested.

mode

Single character string, compared to mode(data). Several values always give a problem, since mode(data) is a single string. NULL: mode not tested.

length

Single integer value, compared to length(data). NULL: length not tested.

prop

Single logical value. If TRUE, data must be of type "double", with all its values in [-1, 1], or in [0, 1] with neg_values = FALSE. To also check the class of a proportion object (a matrix for instance), use a second arg_check() call with prop = FALSE.

options

Vector of character strings or integers: the allowed values of data. Numbers of type "double" (in options or data) are accepted if they are integer values, up to a tolerance of about 1.5e-8 (e.g., 0.57 * 100, slightly below 57). NULL: values not tested.

double_as_integer_allowed

Single logical value. If TRUE, class = "integer" and typeof = "integer" also accept a data of type "double" made of integer values (e.g., data = 1). See the details for approximate integers and dates.

all_options_in_data

Single logical value. If FALSE, data must be made of some of the options elements and nothing else (e.g., data = c(1, 1, 2) with options = c(1, 2, 3)). If TRUE, data must contain all the options elements at least once, and nothing else (e.g., data = c(1, 1, 2, 3)). Ignored if options is NULL.

na_contain

Single logical value. Can data contain NA?

neg_values

Single logical value. Are negative values authorized? Warning: TRUE (default) means that no check is performed. FALSE requires the typeof argument set to "double" or "integer", the mode argument set to "numeric", or prop = TRUE (error otherwise). A factor tested with typeof or mode then gives the problem "... MUST BE MADE OF NON NEGATIVE VALUES BUT IS A FACTOR".

inf_values

Single logical value. Are infinite values (Inf, -Inf) authorized? Warning: TRUE (default) means that no check is performed. FALSE requires the typeof argument set to "double" or the mode argument set to "numeric" (error otherwise). A factor then gives the problem "... MUST BE MADE OF NON INFINITE VALUES BUT IS A FACTOR".

print

Single logical value. If TRUE, the text of the problems is also displayed (with message()) when $problem is TRUE. FALSE by default, to let the calling function handle the problems (see the examples).

data_name

Single character string: name of the tested object in the returned text. If NULL, the expression passed to data is used.

data_arg

Single logical value. Is the tested object an argument of a function? "ARGUMENT" (TRUE, default) or "OBJECT" is written in the returned text.

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used. Only checked and used when safer_check is TRUE.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages and to the returned text (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

A list:

  • problem: single logical value, TRUE if a problem is detected.

  • text: the problems detected (text starting with "ERROR"), or a text saying that no problem is detected.

  • object_name: data_name if provided, otherwise the expression passed to data as a string (e.g., "vec1").

Details

At least one of class, typeof, mode, length, options and prop = TRUE must be set. options and prop = TRUE exclude each other, and require class, typeof and mode to be NULL. length can be combined with all of them. Wrong argument values or combinations raise an error.

The function tests what is written, even if incoherent: arg_check(data = factor(1), class = "factor", mode = "character") returns a problem, since factors are of mode "numeric".

To accept several possibilities for the tested object, combine several arg_check() calls:


tempo1 <- saferDev::arg_check(data = data, mode = "character")
tempo2 <- saferDev::arg_check(data = data, class = "factor")
tempo3 <- saferDev::arg_check(data = data, class = "integer")
if(tempo1$problem == TRUE & tempo2$problem == TRUE & tempo3$problem == TRUE){
    print("data ARGUMENT MUST BE A VECTOR OF (1) STRINGS, (2) FACTORS OR (3) INTEGERS")
}

Warning: double_as_integer_allowed = TRUE only accepts exact integer values stored as double: approximate integers (e.g., 1 + 1e-10 or 3 - 1e-10) are problems. Objects of type "double" that are not numeric (e.g., dates) are problems when tested with options, and are not accepted as integers by double_as_integer_allowed = TRUE.

See also

class, typeof, mode.

Author

Gael Millot

Haiding Wang

Examples

# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/arg_check.html
test <- base::matrix(data = 1:3, nrow = 3, ncol = 1, byrow = FALSE, dimnames = NULL)
# $problem is TRUE: class(test) is c("matrix", "array"), compared exactly to the class argument
saferDev::arg_check(data = test, class = "vector", typeof = NULL, mode = "numeric", length = NULL,
    prop = FALSE, options = NULL, double_as_integer_allowed = FALSE, all_options_in_data = FALSE,
    na_contain = FALSE, neg_values = TRUE, inf_values = TRUE, print = TRUE, data_name = NULL,
    data_arg = TRUE, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> 
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> ERROR
#> 
#> THE test ARGUMENT MUST BE CLASS vector
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> $problem
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $text
#> [1] "ERROR\n\nTHE test ARGUMENT MUST BE CLASS vector"
#> 
#> $object_name
#> [1] "test"
#> 
# $problem is TRUE as well, for the same reason
saferDev::arg_check(data = test, class = "matrix", typeof = NULL, mode = "numeric", length = NULL,
    prop = FALSE, options = NULL, double_as_integer_allowed = FALSE, all_options_in_data = FALSE,
    na_contain = FALSE, neg_values = TRUE, inf_values = TRUE, print = TRUE, data_name = NULL,
    data_arg = TRUE, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
#> 
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> ERROR
#> 
#> THE test ARGUMENT MUST BE CLASS matrix
#> 
#> ================
#> 
#> $problem
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $text
#> [1] "ERROR\n\nTHE test ARGUMENT MUST BE CLASS matrix"
#> 
#> $object_name
#> [1] "test"
#> 
# $problem is FALSE (error_text is added to the returned text)
saferDev::arg_check(data = test, class = base::c("matrix", "array"), typeof = NULL,
    mode = "numeric", length = NULL, prop = FALSE, options = NULL,
    double_as_integer_allowed = FALSE, all_options_in_data = FALSE, na_contain = FALSE,
    neg_values = TRUE, inf_values = TRUE, print = TRUE, data_name = NULL, data_arg = TRUE,
    safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = " using saferDev::arg_check()")
#> $problem
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $text
#> [1] "NO PROBLEM DETECTED FOR THE test ARGUMENT using saferDev::arg_check()"
#> 
#> $object_name
#> [1] "test"
#> 
# Inside a function, with print = FALSE (default): the function stops with the returned text
fun1 <- function(x){
    tempo <- saferDev::arg_check(data = x, class = NULL, typeof = "double", mode = NULL,
        length = 1, prop = FALSE, options = NULL, double_as_integer_allowed = FALSE,
        all_options_in_data = FALSE, na_contain = FALSE, neg_values = FALSE, inf_values = TRUE,
        print = FALSE, data_name = NULL, data_arg = TRUE, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
        error_text = "")
    if(tempo$problem == TRUE){
        base::stop(tempo$text, call. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
    }
    base::return(x)
}
fun1(x = 2)
#> [1] 2
base::try(expr = fun1(x = -2), silent = FALSE,
    outFile = base::getOption(x = "try.outFile", default = base::stderr()))
#> Error : ERROR
#> 
#> THE x ARGUMENT MUST BE MADE OF NON NEGATIVE VALUES.
